A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepFlow work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A.1–A.8 are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet class-conditional generation, MS-COCO and GenEval text-to-image results, component ablations, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a 600-epoch DeepFlow result in Table 4.

M1.justification: The transformer branches, deep supervision, VeRA acceleration MLP, time-gap conditioning, cross-space attention, training losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet at 256×256 and 512×512 for class-conditional generation, MS-COCO for text-to-image generation, and zero-shot GenEval. The additional training-budget result introduces no new dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: The reported comparator sets remain unchanged, including SiT and SSL-aligned variants and the autoregressive, masked-generation, and diffusion baselines in Tables 4–5. Additional citations in v2 do not introduce evaluated baseline rows.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds a 600-epoch training condition for DeepFlow-XL/2-3T without SSL alignment alongside the retained 400-epoch condition. Existing data splits, metrics, sampling procedures, and model configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component, time-gap, acceleration-design, and efficiency analyses in Tables 7–8 are retained. Appendix feature-distance, VeRA-design, sampling-step, CFG-scale, and qualitative analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Figure 7's mean and standard deviation across sampling-step settings. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds a 600-epoch DeepFlow-XL/2-3T result: FID 1.89, sFID 4.40, and IS 263.3. The 400-epoch result remains 1.97, 4.39, and 264.7, respectively. This is an additional training-budget condition, not a revision of the existing result; other reported results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), including the flow-matching formulation, deep-supervision loss, second-order acceleration objective, and total loss, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and claims about internal velocity alignment, eightfold faster convergence, generation quality, and text-to-image performance. The shortened conclusion preserves their meaning.

C2.justification: Explanations of feature alignment, component benefits, and training efficiency are retained. Appendix A.8 still identifies weaker text-to-image performance than leading models and the need for larger-scale training and deeper theoretical understanding.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.3 retain the same implementation, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, A100 hardware, mixed-precision, and sampling details. Dataset access information and the project link are unchanged; no additional implementation guidance accompanies the new result.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to FlowTok, Grouping First, Attending Smartly, MaskBit, and Randomized Autoregressive Visual Generation in Sections 2 and 4.2.1. The central positioning relative to SiT, REPA, and deep supervision remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are small wording edits in related work, the state-of-the-art comparison paragraph, and the conclusion. The section hierarchy, explanations, and overall narrative remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains one row, Figure 3 is slightly resized, and text and tables reflow, including Table 1 moving from page 6 to page 5. The conclusion fits on page 8 and the appendix starts earlier; the existing figures and qualitative samples are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional 600-epoch result modestly improves documentation of the training-budget tradeoff beyond v1's 400-epoch result: it reports lower FID but slightly worse sFID and IS at a larger budget. This provides limited useful evidence without changing the method or resolving the existing limitations, so the overall gain is small.
